newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed, gas oil weak.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed, gas oil weak.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Tuesday, traders said.

Traders said Italy's ISAB cut crude throughput by 10 to 20 percent at its 220,000 bpd Melilli refinery in Sicily due to poor refining margins. But output of refined products would not be affected, a trader familiar with Isab's operations said, as crude throughputs could be replaced with other feedstocks.
Other Med refiners were heard considering refinery run cuts too.
Jet markets were long and sellers were eyeing arbitrage options.
Firm Far East markets were the main focus, but many traders expected demand to initially be filled out of the Mid-East Gulf.
They said Libyan barrels were asking around cif high $2 a tonne with EC material asking around cif high +$4/5 cif Med.

Gas oil continued weak with growing avails keeping the pressure on benchmark quotes. Traders said weaker NWE markets had also compounded the effect of slack local demand although many were looking for "stop loss" arbitrage to the North.
Premiums for Russian remained under pressure from good avails and with hefty avails out of the Baltic cramping trade to the North. Cargoes were valued around cif high -$1.50 cif Med.
FOD and diesel cargo differentials were also weak at around 50 cents to $1 a tonne under benchmark quotes.
Gasoline held steady, still supported by east Med and U.S. demand, and tight low octane supplies due refinery maintenance.
Naphtha was steady to higher as traders awaited the fate of several large cargoes to be loaded out of Skikda this month.
A 60,000 tonne cargo is expected to load on Wednesday and at least two more co-loaded cargoes, possibly three, were seen out of Skikda in February. High freight rates have forced the large cargoes.
